input:
Safety stock for the spare motor is 4448 units. The stock is held against variation in demand during the replenishment lead time, at a 95% cycle service level, and the figure follows from the demand and lead time stated below.

Demand for the spare motor averages 3708 units per week, with a standard deviation of 953 units per week. The replenishment lead time is 8 weeks. Safety stock is sized on the variation of demand over the whole lead time, not on the variation of a single week: weekly variations partly cancel across the lead time, and the stock covers the spread of total lead-time demand that remains. At a 95% cycle service level, lead-time demand is met from stock in all but a small minority of replenishment cycles, and the 4448 units are the quantity that the stated demand spread requires for that service level.

The policy treats demand as normal and independent between weeks. Independence is what allows the weekly variations to cancel in part; if demand in successive weeks moved together, the spread of lead-time demand would be wider than the policy assumes, and the same stock would deliver a lower service level than the one stated. Seasonal peaks are excluded from the policy. No additional stock is held for peak periods, and a seasonal peak that falls inside a replenishment lead time draws on the same safety stock as any other week. The policy therefore states a service level for ordinary demand variation across the year, and it leaves peak cover to be decided separately if operating experience shows the exclusion is not tenable.
